message.content: 獅子（屬於貓科）與斑馬（屬於馬科）雖然都屬於哺乳類，但它們在進化樹上相距較遠。兩者最早的共同祖先可以追溯到**古獸亞門（Laurasiatheria）**的祖先，這是一個大約七千萬年前出現的哺乳動物群體。換句話說，獅子和斑馬的共同祖先是屬於古獸亞門的一種早期哺乳動物，而非更近的家族或科。

Probably mention that lions and zebras share a common ancestor within the order Carnivora? Actually lions are felids, zebras are equids. They diverged from a common ancestor in the family level? They share a common ancestor at the level of the order Carnivora? Wait, lions are mammals, specifically within the family Felidae. Zebras are mammals, within Equidae. Both belong to the order Perissodactyla? No, lions are Artiodactyla? Actually lions are in order Carnivora, suborder Feliformia. Zebras are in order Perissodactyla, suborder Hippomorpha. So they diverged earlier. Their common ancestor would be a mammal from the clade Laurasiatheria? They share a common ancestor at the level of the class Mammalia. But maybe the question expects "Mammals" or "Mammalian ancestor". Or maybe "the last common ancestor of all placental mammals" or "the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae" which is the ancestor of the order Carnivora and Perissodactyla. That would be the ancestor of the clade Laurasiatheria. So answer: The last common ancestor of lions and zebras was a mammal that lived around 70 million years ago, belonging to the clade Laurasiatheria. So answer accordingly.
